book.magitech.glistening_lexicon.spark_o: Chapter 0: Spark of Technology
Introduction

Magitech is a project exploring an innovative world that fuses magic and technology.
The project's ultimate goal is to formalize and utilize all mana-derived magical forces, transitioning from empirical practice to theory.

All magical forces will be studied as physical phenomena and applied to enable the development of new devices and equipment.
This chapter introduces the basic concepts frequently used in Magitech.
Tool Crafting

By combining multiple parts you can create more complex and powerful tools. These tools possess properties different from those made by standard crafting.
Tool creation requires specific materials and special workbenches to cut out and assemble parts.

The following explanations use a wand as an example; the method for creating a wand will be described.
First, prepare the two required workbenches below.

This is the workbench used to cut out parts. Most parts require several materials, and the number varies by part type.
To cut a part, place materials on the workbench and select the desired part on the bench.
This is the workbench for assembling tools from parts. Arrange the required parts for the tool in any order to assemble it.
Creating a wand requires four parts: catalyst, conductor, light handle, and fastener. Cut each part out and place them on the workbench to assemble the wand.

Materials are generally obtained from natural resources like ores and wood. Here, stripped logs, copper, iron ingots, and fluorite are recommended.
You don't need to unify materials across the whole tool; different parts can use different materials.
However, using different materials may affect the wand's performance, for better or worse.

A light melee weapon allowing quick attacks. Its lightness grants fast attack speed and easier dodging.
However, its per-hit damage is low and reach short, making it disadvantageous against heavily armored or fast enemies.

A standard melee weapon with balanced performance. It offers a good balance of damage and attack speed, suitable against various enemies.
However, it may be inferior to specialized weapons.

A heavy melee weapon with high attack power and defense. Its powerful single strikes are effective against slow enemies.
However, its slow attack speed and reduced evasiveness make it weak against flurrying or ranged foes. Also, being specialized for physical attacks, it is not suited for elemental attacks.

A common mining tool that efficiently mines ores and stones. It has fast mining speed and is suited for detailed mining work.
However, its attack power is low and it's relatively unsuitable for combat.

A tool that delivers wide-area impacts, suitable for construction and mining. It can mine multiple rocks at once.
However, it's slow in attack speed and unsuited for fine work.
A relatively heavy melee weapon suited for felling wood. It has high attack power and slightly longer reach. It also efficiently chops wood.
A light mining tool that efficiently digs dirt and sand. It has fast mining speed, defensive attributes, and wide attack range. Its attack power is low and not well-suited for combat.

A tool that can sweep a wide area, suitable for harvesting grass and crops. It has wide attack range and reach, allowing multiple targets to be hit at once. Since it's inferior in physical attacks, an elemental attack-focused build is recommended.
A common handheld tool for using magic; it can use magics inscribed on thread pages. It can also be used when held in the off-hand.

A tool that allows the use of more powerful magic than a wand.
It is more powerful than a wand, but has a slower casting speed.
Like a wand, it can be used to cast the magics engraved on thread pages.
Tool Belt

With diversified tools, switching between them becomes frequent. The tool belt is a convenient piece of equipment to quickly switch tools. Holding the key to open the tool belt displays a list of equipped tools you can select to switch; refer to key bindings for details.
It becomes usable when equipped in the belt slot. The tool belt can store all tools, including fishing rods.
Magic

Magic is one means of utilizing magical power, including mana. Using magic requires tools like wands, thread pages, and threadbound items. These tools function as media to supply mana needed to produce magic's effects.

This lexicon incorporates threadbound functionality and can use magics inscribed on thread pages. Thread pages determine the form of a magic and are stored within threadbound items. Using a wand allows you to use magic inscribed on a thread page.

Place this lexicon in the 'Threadbound' slot of your inventory and open the radial spell menu to see the list of available magics. To use a magic, select an appropriate thread page and use a wand to consume mana and activate the magic. See keybindings for details.
Thread Page

Each thread page has an element and a shape. The element determines the fundamental nature of the magic, and the shape determines effect range and activation method. Various magics exist from combinations of elements and shapes.
This book initially contains an 'Enercrux' and a random thread page.
Spell Conversion
Magic can be used to alter the properties of matter. When using a wand, this is generally called infusion or spell conversion. Spell conversion is essential for creating basic magical devices.
You can perform spell conversion by applying magic to dropped items. Doing spell conversion requires using a wand to perform specific magics.
Wood used in basic devices. Its dark red color is characteristic and its bark is hard and brittle like scales.
A stone containing magical energy. Used as device casing; it is elastic and relatively tough.
Fluorite with high mana concentration. Breaking it supplies mana to nearby things. When mana production devices are lacking, it can serve as a power source for devices.
book.magitech.glistening_lexicon.systema: Chapter 1: Systematic Miracle
Infusion Techniques

This chapter explains basic processing techniques. Basic processing mainly injects mana into materials to obtain desired materials.
This processing plays an important role in creating complex devices and applying magic.

To perform infusion processing, first create a device called an Infusion Altar.
The Infusion Altar injects mana into materials and is central to basic processing techniques.

Use an Enercrux or Charged Fluorite on the altar to supply mana and place base materials on the altar to begin processing.
All infusion processing requires mana supply; if mana supply is insufficient, processing stops.
If additional materials are required, place pedestal pillars around the altar and put the extra materials on them to perform infusion processing.

The primary products of infusion processing are Aspect Crystals and High Purity Fluorite.
Aspect Crystals are each associated with specific concepts and play important roles in magical applications; there are many types and they are documented separately.
High Purity Fluorite is a high-grade fluorite that contains mana at high concentration and is used as a power source, core, or base material.
Aspect Crystal
Aspect Crystals encapsulate an alchemical aspect into a crystal. These crystals make energy extraction easy and safe to store, and are applied in many contexts.

They are mainly used as power sources or catalysts for functional devices. Aspect Crystals are created by infusion; required materials vary by type. Given material flexibility, it's recommended to craft them using locally available resources.
A crystal that constantly emits heat, with flame-like flicker within. Crystallizes the concept of heat. Used for smelting and as a source of propulsion.
A crystal that solidifies surrounding matter. Very pure and transparent. Crystallizes the concept of fixation. Used for refining and cooling.
A crystal that slowly discharges and occasionally emits sparks. Crystallizes conduction. Used as a powerful power source or for electrical supply.
A translucent crystal emitting strange light that causes objects to appear different; crystallizes illusion. Used in defensive confusion devices and optical equipment.
A crystal that vibrates at low frequency and emits low tones, disorienting nearby creatures. Crystallizes vibration. Used for demolition and as sensor power.
A crystal with mysterious power that inspires ideas. Crystallizes arcana; used as a basis for magical devices and as a magical catalyst.
A wind-wreathed crystal that sometimes functions as a pump. Crystallizes flow; used for fluid control, pump power, and propulsion.
A crystal that distorts surrounding space, appearing and disappearing suddenly. Crystallizes spacetime; used to generate spatial anomalies, portals, and teleportation catalysts.
Mana Transport

Mana can be transported using dedicated devices, just like other matter and energy.
There are various types of transport devices; here we describe the most basic ones.
Mana transport consists of three types: devices that supply mana, devices that receive mana, and devices that form the transport path.

Generally, mana flows from devices with a higher fill ratio relative to their capacity to those with a lower one.
Exceptions: mana-producing devices always output, and mana-consuming devices always draw. Mana-holding devices have a flow limit and cannot transport beyond that rate. Devices that form the transport path have no flow limit.
A Mana Vessel is a mana storage device with connectors for input and output. Placing it directly beneath an Infusion Altar allows it to automatically replenish mana during processing.
A Mana Node is a device that can wirelessly transport mana to distant Mana Nodes or Mana Relays. It can also bridge wired and wireless connections such as a Mana Vessel's connector.
A Mana Relay can wirelessly transport mana to distant Mana Nodes or Mana Relays. It cannot connect to connectors, but can transmit over longer distances than a Mana Node.
Fluid Alchemy
Alchemy generally refers to chemical reactions that utilize mana. Here we deal with liquid alchemy. This requires dedicated apparatus and a mana supply system.
This cauldron has a connector that supplies mana and can add energy to internal liquids and solids to trigger special reactions.

In fluid alchemy, potions serve as primary ingredients. Various potions can be created by adding materials to water or base potions; many grant special effects when consumed.
Mana Potions are the most basic and are used in most alchemical processes, being liquids rich in mana.
Such special liquids cannot be stored in ordinary glass. Therefore, use special glass bottles that block mana energy. This material can also be made via liquid alchemy.
A special bottle that blocks mana, primarily used to store potions and highly reactive liquids.
Potions
Besides Mana Potions, there are various potions that can be produced using Mana Potions as a base. Here we describe aspect potions, healing potions, and sulfuric acid.

Aspect potions can temporarily increase the magic output of the corresponding element when consumed. Until advanced facilities are available, this use is common. If you want to deal more magical damage, this is very effective.
A potion containing the Ember aspect. It emits heat and can temporarily provide Ember aspect. It radiates energy to the surrounding area and is highly reactive on its own.

A potion containing the Glace aspect. It feels as cold as ice to the touch but does not freeze the bottle. It can temporarily supply the Glace aspect and can be controlled in natural conditions to rapidly transfer heat and solidify surroundings.

A potion containing the Surge aspect. If leaked, it will begin to discharge and can temporarily supply Surge aspect. It has a destructive force without intent; handle with care to prevent unintended chaining.
A potion containing the Phantom aspect. It constantly emits a faint light and can temporarily provide the Phantom aspect. It rarely causes physical effects but may distort the user's perception.

A potion containing the Tremor aspect. It vibrates irregularly and can temporarily supply Tremor aspect. It constantly seeks destruction and may explode if stored in thin bottles or materials without resistance.

A potion containing the Magic aspect. It emits mysterious sounds and light and can temporarily supply the Magic aspect. Among aspect potions, it is the safest to store and suffers minimal energy loss.
A potion containing the Flow aspect. It violently convects and can temporarily supply the Flow aspect. It generates air currents and expands its effect by splashing.

A potion containing the Hollow aspect. It occasionally distorts the space inside the container and can temporarily provide the Hollow aspect. If not properly sealed, it may form small portals and vanish.

A potion with healing effects. As a medical method it is imperfect and may cause abnormal tissue growth with strange organs. However, it is extremely useful when injured and is often used on the front lines.

A very powerful acid. A fundamental liquid for chemical reactions that instantly alters substances it touches. By immersing multiple types of metal plates, it is possible to generate electric current.
Tool Traits

The materials used in a tool each have unique effects. These effects are called traits, and they have a noticeable influence on how the tool performs.
Understanding and combining traits appropriately allows the same tool to perform more powerfully.

A tool's traits are determined by the materials used for its parts. Regardless of where a material is used, its traits affect the entire tool. You can view a material's traits from its parts or from the tools that use it.
Repairing

Assembled tools lose durability with use and eventually become broken.
Broken tools are not destroyed but cannot be used until repaired.

A workbench for performing repairs. To repair, you need one of the materials used in the tool and an iron ingot.
Five repairs will fully restore durability.
Repeatedly repairing and using the same tool increases its proficiency and can raise base stats. Required proficiency and Tier depend on how the tool was obtained and how many upgrades it has.
A workbench for enhancing tools. Three stats are randomly selected from a tool's stats, and one can be improved. Enhancements require materials corresponding to the tool's Tier.
book.magitech.glistening_lexicon.potenti: Chapter 2: Mana Mechanisms & Potential Control
High-Pressure Materials

This chapter explains automation for processing and transport. Chapter 1 covered manual processing; automation enables more efficient processing and transport.
Automation requires materials that can withstand higher mana potentials.

These materials can be produced via standard infusion processing; methods are described on the following pages. High-pressure materials tolerate high mana potentials, enabling higher-efficiency transport and advanced processing.
A stone that helps regulate mana flow; used as a base material for enhanced devices. A crystalline stone formulation that maximizes fluorite's buffering effect.
A metal woven with strands. Used as frame material and decoration for enhanced devices. Strand induction strongly controls the direction of mana movement.
Magical Accessories

Magical accessories enhance devices related to magic and other arcane functions or provide new features. Rings, for example, can amplify magic effects or reduce mana required for casting. Some increase defense or reduce fall damage. Rings using strands amplify magic output.
Here we describe how to create a Fluxium ring. Fluxium rings can be made easily using workbenches and infusion processing.
Enhanced Mana Machines
Using materials that withstand high mana potentials allows for more advanced processing and faster transport. Enhanced mana machines are improved versions of the basic devices described in Chapter 1.
Mana Production
By using advanced materials, devices can automatically collect and produce mana. This stabilizes mana supply and enables automation of many devices.
A device that collects mana from the air. If multiple such devices exist nearby, they will compete and efficiency will decrease.
A device that consumes Ember aspect to perform fast refining; as a byproduct it produces large amounts of mana.
Advanced Mana Transfer
In addition to basic mana transport, firing mana as projectiles allows transportation over greater distances. This method is implemented by a launcher and a receiver.
Launches mana as projectiles that can transport mana rapidly over long distances.
A device that absorbs mana projectiles and supplies the received mana to other devices.
A branching point for wired connections. Connectors are present on all faces.
Sucks mana in from one side and emits it from the other. Can be turned off with a redstone signal.
Item Transport
This section describes item transport. The primary method uses mana projectiles.
A device that binds items to passing mana projectiles and transports them to their destination, taking items from connected containers.
A device that receives items bound to passing mana projectiles and places them into connected containers.
Collects dropped items and inserts them into connected containers. Consumes mana when active.
Automatic Production

Use mana-powered devices to automate material processing.
Here we describe new processing methods.
A device that grinds materials into powder.

A device that compresses materials into dense lumps.
Compressed materials have denser and stronger properties.
